Q1: Sodium octadecanoate presents known significant hazards for environmental exposure and dermal/eye contact, classified as Tier 1. However, a comprehensive hazard assessment is limited by data deficiencies (Tier 4) for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive hazards (CMR), endocrine disruption (EDC), inhalation (IHL), oral (ORL), and organ/systemic hazards (OGN).
Q2: Sodium octadecanoate is not listed among chemicals of concern. It is recognized on the SCIL Green Circle list as a substance of low concern and is included in the FDA's inventory of Substances Added to Food, suggesting it is generally considered to have a favorable safety profile.
Q3: With 15,000 scientific literature references, Sodium octadecanoate is relatively well-studied compared to many materials in the fracking and petrochemical sector, possessing a clearly defined molecular formula and substance class. However, its hazard profile remains incomplete, as five out of seven hazard classes are currently data deficient (Tier 4).
